newsitem.title: USA: Aviator on Earhart flight lands in Africa.
newsitem.headline: Aviator on Earhart flight lands in Africa.

text.p: A Texas businesswoman and aviator who is retracing the flight of the legendary Amelia Earhart crossing the Atlantic Ocean, touching down on Friday in Dakar, Senegal, a spokeswoman said.
The Atlantic crossing -- from Natal, Brazil, to Dakar -- took Linda Finch nearly 13 hours aboard her 1935 Lockheed Electra 10E, the same model used by Earhart in 1937.
"The flight across the Atlantic was very uneventful," said spokeswoman Jennifer Riggs. Finch saw only two ships during the crossing. "It was just dark," Riggs said.
From Dakar, Finch was scheduled to continue on to Las Palmas, Spain, on Saturday.

Finch, a 46-year-old San Antonio businesswoman, took off from Oakland, California, on March 17 at the start of the 30,000-mile (48,000 km), 2 1/2 month trip that follows a route similar to Earhart's 1937 flight.
Earhart, the first woman to fly solo across the Atlantic, completed 22,000 miles (35,400 km) of her journey and vanished in July 1937 on the leg from New Guinea to Howland Island.
Finch's journey, called "World Flight 1997," will span five continents and include more than 30 stops in 20 countries. She is expected to return to Oakland in late May.
